info.title: notefeed API
info.description:
Post markdown notes to a feed, read them back. See https://docs.notefeed.me/

Every error is JSON, `{"error": "...", "code": "..."}`. Besides the responses listed per operation, an unknown path under /api/v1 answers 404 (`not_found`) and a method an operation doesn't have answers 405 with `Allow`.

tags.name: Feeds
tags.description: By the feed's name, the write key. Need the instance password when one is set.

tags.name: Read
tags.description: By the feed's read id. Public and read-only.

post.description: The body is the note, a file, and `Content-Type` says which kind: `text/markdown` (UTF-8, at most 102400 bytes), or an image, `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif` or `image/webp` (at most NOTEFEED_MAX_IMAGE_BYTES, default 5 MiB). Nothing is guessed: any other type, or none, is `415`, and so is a body that is not what the type says (an image is recognized by its first bytes; SVG is refused). It is stored byte for byte, with no resizing and no metadata stripped (EXIF such as GPS position stays in an image). Creates the feed with its first note, optionally protected by its own password (`X-Feed-Password`; 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters, with no space at the start or end) and with the read id in `X-Read-Id`; both are only used by the post that creates the feed. Where licenses are sold, the post that creates the feed can bring a license key in `X-License-Key`, with or without a password; a feed password needs one, or the post is refused with `402`. Posting to a protected feed needs its password. Also served at `POST /{feed}`, the short form curl one-liners use. The response names the note's `file` and where it is served, `file_url`, under the feed's read id (public like the read link). Metadata goes in headers: `X-Note-Title`, `X-Note-Tags` (at most 10 tags, each 1 to 32 characters of letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` and `:`; case is folded to lowercase, duplicates are removed), `X-Note-Alt` (images), `X-Note-Name` (the original file name), `X-Note-Date` (where it is placed in the feed: a past date backdates it, a future one schedules it). A markdown note with its pictures is one `multipart/form-data` request: a `text` part (the markdown, a field or a file part; a file part keeps its line breaks, a field's are sent as CRLF), `file` parts (up to 10 pictures, each with its file name and image `Content-Type`) and `alt.<file name>` fields. The pictures are stored first, each as its own note named by its file name, then the text with its references to them (`![](chart.png)`, `[x]: chart.png`, as written or percent-decoded) swapped for the stored files; a picture it never refers to is appended as `![](file)`. Everything is checked before the first write, and a failed write removes what the request stored: all or nothing. `X-Note-Alt` and `X-Note-Name` are 400. The answer has `attachments`, the stored pictures in the order of the `file` parts. The `text` part is optional: `X-Note-Title` goes on the text note, `X-Note-Tags` on every note, `X-Note-Date` on the text note (its pictures take the milliseconds just before it); with no `text` part only the pictures are stored, each with the title, and the answer's top level is the first picture. A refused multipart post that would have created a protected feed creates nothing.

parameters.name: feed
parameters.description: The feed's name. It is the write key: anyone who knows it can post.

parameters.name: X-Feed-Password
parameters.description: The feed's own password, when it has one: to post, list or get, and (as the current password) to change or remove it. On the `POST` that creates a feed it sets the feed's password; on a `POST` to an existing feed that has none it answers 409. An empty value is the same as no header, so a `POST` with an empty one creates an open feed.

parameters.name: X-Read-Id
parameters.description: The read id the feed gets when this post creates it: 3 to 64 characters (a-z, 0-9, - and _), random when left out or empty, ignored for a feed that exists. A short readable one is guessable: protect the feed with a password if that matters. 409 when it is taken

parameters.name: X-License-Key
parameters.description: Only on an instance that sells licenses, on the post that creates the feed: the key of the license to put on the new feed, with or without `X-Feed-Password` (a feed password is for licensed feeds: with one and no key, 402). 400 for a key that is none, 402 for one whose license has lapsed; either way nothing is created. Ignored on an existing feed: put a license on it with `PUT /api/v1/feeds/{feed}/license`

parameters.name: X-Note-Title
parameters.description: The note's title, for a raw body; a JSON or form body's own `title` wins. At most 100 characters, one line, with no control or text-direction override characters.

parameters.name: X-Note-Tags
parameters.description: Tags for the note, comma-separated (`ci,deploy`): at most 10 tags, each 1 to 32 characters of letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` and `:`; case is folded to lowercase, duplicates are removed. For a raw markdown body; a JSON or form body's own `tags` wins. Empty is none.

parameters.name: X-Note-Alt
parameters.description: For an image body: its alternative text; a form's own `alt` wins.

parameters.name: X-Note-Name
parameters.description: The note's file name (at most 200 characters; `/`, `\` and control characters are dropped): for a picture, its original name. The read link serves the newest note with that name at `/r/{readId}/{name}`, a stable address for a file that changes (a name ending in a lower-case extension, such as `post-to-notefeed.md`); a note's own file name (`<id>.<ext>`) comes first

parameters.name: X-Note-Date
parameters.description: An ISO 8601 date and time with its offset (`2026-10-01T09:30:00Z`, `2026-10-01T11:30:00+02:00`) or a date alone (midnight UTC). When the note is placed in the feed, from 1970 to 9999. A time after now schedules it: readers see it from then on. Empty is now.

put.description: The body is the new file, with the same rules as posting: a `Content-Type` that is one of the accepted types, a body that is what it declares. A note keeps its type, so the type must be the note's own (`415` otherwise). Id, creation time and metadata stay: the title of a markdown note without one set follows the new text. Change the title, alt text or tags with `PATCH`. Needs the feed's password if it has one, and counts against the post rate limit. Read links can't edit. A markdown note with its pictures is one `multipart/form-data` request: a `text` part (the markdown, a field or a file part; a file part keeps its line breaks, a field's are sent as CRLF), `file` parts (up to 10 pictures, each with its file name and image `Content-Type`) and `alt.<file name>` fields. The pictures are stored first, each as its own note named by its file name, then the text with its references to them (`![](chart.png)`, `[x]: chart.png`, as written or percent-decoded) swapped for the stored files; a picture it never refers to is appended as `![](file)`. Everything is checked before the first write, and a failed write removes what the request stored: all or nothing. `X-Note-Alt` and `X-Note-Name` are 400. The answer has `attachments`, the stored pictures in the order of the `file` parts. On a `PUT` the `text` part is required and the note must be a markdown note; the note keeps its own title and tags, `X-Note-Tags` goes on the new pictures. A raw body ignores `X-Note-Tags`. The note is looked up first: a missing note is `404` and an image note `415` whatever the body holds.

An empty value is the same as no header, so a `POST` with an empty one creates an open feed.

parameters.name: X-Note-Tags
parameters.description: Only for a multipart body: the tags go on the new pictures (the note keeps its own). A raw body ignores it. Comma-separated, empty is none.

patch.summary: Change a note's title, alt text, tags or date
patch.description: Sets the note's title, alt text (only for images), tags and/or date. An empty title or alt removes it: a markdown note's title follows its text again. `tags` replaces the whole list (an empty list removes them), with the same rules as on a post. A new date moves the note in the feed, with its attachments; a date after now schedules it. Id and links stay, and so does its RSS item's guid. At least one is needed. Needs the feed's password if it has one, and counts against the post rate limit. Read links can't change notes.

An empty value is the same as no header, so a `POST` with an empty one creates an open feed.

post.description: Reserves the feed name now (ADR 0047): with a password it is protected from its first moment, with a read id it gets that read link. Where licenses are sold a license key is required and goes on the new feed; free feeds start with their first note. A feed that exists is 409. Counts against the post rate limit and the instance's feed cap, like a first post. After it, change the title and description with updateFeed.

put.description: Replaces both the title (at most 100 characters) and the description (at most 500); surrounding whitespace is trimmed and control and text-direction override characters are refused. `show_sender` (default true) shows who posted each note to readers; omitted leaves it as it is. `read_id` gives the feed another read link (3 to 64 characters: a-z, 0-9, - and _; empty for a random one): the old id is freed and answers like an unknown read id until another feed takes it, and the notes are not edited (a relative image link follows the new id, a full URL does not). A short readable read id is guessable, so protect the feed with a password if that matters. An instance can turn chosen read ids off (NOTEFEED_ALLOW_CUSTOM_IDS=0): then only an empty `read_id` is accepted. `image` is the file name `uploadImage` returned for this feed (title image), empty to remove it, or omitted to leave it as it is; any other value is a 400. Needs the feed's password if it has one, and counts against the post rate limit. Only on a feed that exists: it is created by its first note. Read links can't change settings.

On the `POST` that creates a feed it sets the feed's password; on a `POST` to an existing feed that has none it answers 409. An empty value is the same as no header, so a `POST` with an empty one creates an open feed.

The name is free again; a feed created there later gets a new read link, and the old one answers like an unknown one. Needs the feed's password if it has one, and counts against the post rate limit.

put.summary: Set or change a feed's password
put.description: On a protected feed: changes the password, with the current one in `X-Feed-Password`. On an open feed: sets one, with no current password, for whoever calls it. An open feed's name is all that protects it, so whoever knows the name may claim the feed this way. From then on everyone who posts to the feed, reads it by its name or changes it needs the password; the read link and RSS stay open.

put.summary: Put a license on a feed
put.description: Only on an instance that sells licenses (404 elsewhere). Puts the license the key names on the feed, taking it off the feed it was on; a feed that has an active license already answers 400 (take it off first). A feed needs no password for a license. A key notefeed doesn't know is 400 and counts as a failed attempt, like a wrong password. Needs the feed's password if it has one, and counts against the post rate limit. Only on a feed that exists: it is created by its first note, which can bring the key in `X-License-Key`.

parameters.description: The feed's name. It is the write key: anyone who knows it can post.

parameters.name: X-Feed-Password

On the `POST` that creates a feed it sets the feed's password; on a `POST` to an existing feed that has none it answers 409. An empty value is the same as no header, so a `POST` with an empty one creates an open feed.

get.summary: Get one note by its feed's read id
get.description: Public, like the read link. A read id the operator removed is `410`.

parameters.name: readId
parameters.description: The feed's read id, from its read link: 22 random characters, one the feed's owner chose, or the feed's own name for a reserved feed. Read-only; never reveals the name of any other feed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The note's id

404.description: No such note, or a malformed or unknown read id

410.description: The operator removed the feed this read id belonged to (`removed`)

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again

get.description: Generated from the server's route table, with `servers` set to this instance's URL.

id.description: The note's id: 22 random characters (base64url) for notes made here, older notes may have another form; any name without a dot for a file placed by hand. It says nothing about the note's date

type.description: The media type of the note's file: `text/markdown`, `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif` or `image/webp`

file_url.description: Where the note's file is served, absolute, under the feed's read id (public like the read link); null while the feed has no read link

size.description: The size of the note's file in bytes

title.description: The title set for the note, else the first heading or the first non-empty line of a markdown note, else the picture's alt text; may be empty

content.description: The note's text, byte-for-byte as posted: for a text type (markdown) only; absent for a picture

alt.description: Alternative text of an image note, when it has one

name.description: The file name an image was posted with, when it came with one

date.description: Where the note is placed in the feed (UTC): when it was posted, unless a date was given or changed; lists are ordered by it

scheduled.description: Present, and true, when the note's date is after now: it is stored, and readers see it from its date on. Absent for every other note

url.description: The note's page in the web UI

sender.description: Verified sign-in name of the poster; absent when the note was posted without a sign-in

tags.description: Labels the poster gave the note (not verified, and shown to readers like the note itself); empty when none

unreadable.description: Present, and true, for a damaged note: its stored copy can't be decrypted. A list shows it in its place, with its id, file, type and time; its title and tags are empty, its size 0, it has no content, and reading it alone is a 500 with the code `unreadable`. Deleting it works. Absent for every other note

next.description: Pass as `before` for the next (older) page; null on the last page

file.description: The note's file name, `<id>.<extension>`. For an image note, pass it as a feed's `image` setting

text.description: The markdown note (UTF-8): a field, or a file part (its name is ignored; its type, if any, `text/markdown` or `application/octet-stream`) to keep its line breaks as they are, since a form field's are sent as CRLF. At most one; required on a PUT. Its references to the files (`![](chart.png)`, `[x]: chart.png`) are swapped for the stored files; a file it never refers to is appended as `![](file)`

file.description: A picture: up to 10 parts, each with a file name (one path segment, 1 to 200 characters, unique in the request) and its image `Content-Type`. An `alt.<file name>` field gives one its alternative text

code.description: Stable machine-readable code; absent only on a 500

title.description: The note's title, at most 100 characters, one line (control and text-direction override characters are refused); empty or left out means the title is taken from the text (a markdown note) or there is none (an image)

alt.description: Alternative text of an image note, at most 500 characters, one line (control and text-direction override characters are refused)

tags.description: The note's tags, the whole new list (`["ci","done"]`): at most 10 tags, each 1 to 32 characters of letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` and `:`; case is folded to lowercase, duplicates are removed. Empty removes them all; omitted leaves them as they are.

date.description: An ISO 8601 date and time with its offset (`2026-10-01T09:30:00Z`, `2026-10-01T11:30:00+02:00`) or a date alone (midnight UTC). When the note is placed in the feed, from 1970 to 9999. A time after now schedules it: readers see it from then on. The note's attachments move with it.

password.description: The new password: 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters, with no space at the start or end
A password that protects the new feed: 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters, with no space at the start or end. Empty or left out: an open feed

license_key.description: Where licenses are sold, required: the key of the license to put on the new feed

read_id.description: The read id to give the feed (3 to 64 characters of a-z, 0-9, - and _); left out: a random one

key.description: The license key, as the checkout or the receipt gave it

title.description: Display title, at most 100 characters, one line (control and text-direction override characters are refused); empty means none (the feed's name is shown)

description.description: Description, at most 500 characters, one line (control and text-direction override characters are refused); may be empty

image.description: The file name of an image uploaded to this feed (see uploadImage), shown as the feed's title image; empty removes it, omitted leaves it as it is

show_sender.description: Whether readers (RSS, the read API and pages) see who posted each note; omitted leaves it as it is, a new feed starts with true

read_id.description: A new read id (3 to 64 characters: a-z, 0-9, - and _), empty for a random one; omitted leaves it as it is. The old read link stops showing this feed, and may later show another one. Notes are not edited: a relative image link (`![](file)`) follows the new id, a full URL keeps the old one and is yours to change. Reserved feeds keep theirs. 409 when it is taken

cap.description: How many text notes a free feed keeps; past it, each new note drops the oldest one

title.description: Display title, at most 100 characters, one line (control and text-direction override characters are refused); empty means none (the feed's name is shown)

description.description: Description, at most 500 characters, one line (control and text-direction override characters are refused); may be empty

protected.description: Whether the feed has its own password

image_url.description: The feed's title image (absolute URL, served under the read id), or null

free_tier.description: A feed without a license on an instance that sells them: its notes against the free tier's cap. null when no cap applies (a licensed feed, or an instance that sells no licenses)
